content: Count high-card points: Ace = 4, King = 3, Queen = 2, Jack = 1. A full deck holds 40 HCP, so an average hand is 10.
A balanced hand has no void, no singleton, and at most one doubleton — patterns 4-3-3-3, 4-4-3-2, and 5-3-3-2. Balanced hands suit notrump contracts.
When your hand is unbalanced — a long suit or a short suit — distribution matters as much as points. Long trump fits produce extra tricks that raw HCP miss.
Myth: “Only high-card points matter.” Shape counts too. A 5-card major or a big fit can be worth far more than the HCP alone suggest.
♠AK4 ♥Q32 ♦K652 ♣J43: A+K = 7, Q = 2, K = 3, J = 1 → 13 HCP. A balanced 4-3-4-2 hand worth an opening bid.
Add up your honors: 4 for each Ace, 3 for each King, 2 for each Queen, 1 for each Jack.
